title: Signal in the noise
angle: The manual's own printed rules, resolved against 600 GB of NOAA weather reduced in-stream to 4 MB. The only pitch whose five minutes are mostly not the core product.
endline: The manufacturer printed the rule. We only worked out that it applies to you.

slides.text: Climate Fit is built, deploying. The routes are live; the deployed replica carries no climatology yet, so `POST /api/climate/fit` answers *no climatology* today.
slides.sub: Demo it locally, and say that sentence rather than let a judge find it. Everything else on these slides is already true, and measured on 2026-09-20.
notes: Say it once, early, and move on.
Then the product, fast: a friend's motorcycle workshop, 20% of his working time, 400 hours a year. He does not use AI — 95% right and he is liable for the 5%, and one question cost about $4.

"Mechanica makes the manual the answer. The model may emit a page number, and the *server* slices the quote out of the original page. It cannot invent a torque figure, because it is never allowed to type one."

slides.kicker: The noise is the problem, and it is upstream of us

slides.sub: *The row lies about what it is.* Honda files the Gold Wing brochure in the same listing as the owner's manual. Piaggio calls the owner's manual a "use and maintenance booklet". `doctype.py` classifies 8 document kinds from the URL and title alone — *never by downloading*.
notes: Nobody publishes a dataset of manuals. We built one adapter per portal, and the registry that came out is a dataset-quality problem in miniature.

*The file lies about being a manual.* Of 773 ingest attempts, 38 URLs were 3-page flyers and 23 were not PDFs at all. The pipeline rejects them on page count and magic bytes and writes the reason down: 648 done, 80 error, 24 duplicate, 21 suspicious.
*Retraction.* A portal that drops a model must be able to un-say it — a retracted row stops being advertised instead of lingering as a dead link.
We copy no manuals at crawl time. RegistryEntry has no field that could hold one.

slides.sub: Then we asked one question of that corpus: *how many of these manuals print a rule that depends on where the vehicle actually is?* — **522 of 529. 98.7%.** The manual knows the rule. It has no idea whether it applies to you. *NOAA does.*
notes: "They turned unstructured documents into something you could actually query." That is what should land here.

The grounding gate is the load-bearing part: a quote that cannot be found in the PDF text layer is dropped, and the log says how many. On this corpus, 290 of 110,094 sections dropped (0.3%) and 0 of 431,292 highlights discarded.
Clause families: road salt / coastal 518 manuals · dusty / sandy 487 · antifreeze 394 · wet / muddy 371 · ambient temperature 340.

slides.title: The noisy half, and the curated half
slides.caption: The manual's own printed rules on one side, public weather reduced in-stream on the other, and a verdict that costs zero tokens.
notes: *The cleaning is small and decisive.* ISD puts a quality code at character 93. Re-running the reduction with that filter off, over 400 station-years: only *0.12%* of readings are flagged — but at Russian station 263240-99999 the 2024 minimum moves from −21.5 °C to −25.1 °C. A 0.12% cleaning step decides the answer. *That is the whole challenge in one line.*

*The join is where we actually got burned.* Our first pass matched stations by name: "Boston" landed on a buoy, "Moscow" on Moscow Idaho, "Chicago" on a Canadian station reporting −46.9 °C. The shipped join is geodesic, filters the 16,885 stations that stopped reporting, and prints the distance.
Do not imply we swept all 600 GB. Say which slice ran: one full year, 2024. Six years is the same command with --years 2019:2024.

slides.label: 227 manuals · 9 markets · 4 makes · model years 2006–2026
slides.sub: Every one of them prints *the same antifreeze floor*, on 1,028 distinct pages. Spread *0.0000* — zero variance. Somebody in Austria typed it once, and it shipped to every market on earth.
notes: Of the eight rule types we extract, antifreeze_floor is the *only* one with a spread of 0.0. Cold-start, dusty, wet, salt and heat clauses spread 0.74–0.85 across makes.
*The one rule the whole industry agrees on is the one that is wrong for a fifth of the planet's weather stations.*
The earlier 206 came from the 508 spec files; same finding, smaller denominator. Both scripts are in the repo.

slides.title: How often is that wrong?
slides.line: We no longer sample. This is the whole 2024 population — 10,715 usable station-years.
head: stations recording a 2024 temperature below…
share

cells: *−25 °C — the floor every one of those 227 manuals prints*

slides.note: *Say the denominator.* That is 20.7% of the world's *actively reporting weather stations*, not 20.7% of riders — and ISD station density is heavy in the US, Russia and Canada. To make a rider-weighted claim we would need registrations, and we do not have them. *And 113 of the breaching stations sit above 1,500 m* — the manual's single number fails on the vertical axis too.
notes: The seeded 260-station draw we quoted before reproduces exactly off the rebuilt data — 210 usable, 48 breaching, 22.9% — so the estimator was unbiased and the population number is the one to use now.
*Do not say "22.9% of riders".* It is 22.9% of actively reporting weather stations, and the sample is biased toward the US, Russia and Canada.

The unexpected part: Tibetan-plateau stations at 4,613 m and 4,535 m, a US station at 4,113 m, Tajikistan at 3,940 m. Those are *altitude* stations, not latitude ones — which is why altitude became its own rule type.

left.label: Minneapolis
left.caption: MINNEAPOLIS–ST PAUL INTL · 10.8 km · ENGINE OIL GRADE, action needed · 20.7% of readings below 0 °C · p. 215

right.label: International Falls, MN

slides.caption: Then *tap the coolant row*: the PDF opens on p. 215 with "Antifreeze protection to at least −25 °C" highlighted. *KTM said it. We only worked out that it applies to you.*
notes: Then change it to Bangkok: every cold rule goes grey and the dust rule lights up. *The negative control is part of the demo on purpose.* Bangkok, Dubai, Miami and Delhi are negative controls in CI — if a cold rule ever fires there, the join is broken.
KTM does print a temperature-banded oil grade: *"Engine oil grade at ambient temperature ≥ 0 °C: SAE 10W/50; < 0 °C: SAE 5W/40"*, KTM 1390 Super Adventure R 2026 US, p. 215.
Phoenix 0.0% below 0 °C · Zurich 6.1% · Minneapolis 20.7% · International Falls 34.6% · Bangkok 0.0%.

The close: "the manual is still the only thing we show you. What the manufacturer could never print is *whether the rule is about you* — and that took 600 GB of somebody else's data to answer, reduced to 4.34 MB, for zero tokens and three to six milliseconds a look."

slides.title: voloridge.md — check this list the morning of

groups.label: This pitch
items: Do not say Climate Fit is deployed and working. The routes are live, the climatology is not in the replica.
Do not say "22.9% of riders" — it is 22.9% of actively reporting weather stations, and the sample is biased toward the US, Russia and Canada.
Do not imply we swept all 600 GB. Say which slice ran: 2024.
Do not quote the † numbers (the hand-labelled precision/recall) as measured.
Do not claim a failure rate from running the wrong coolant — we have exposure data, not outcome data.

groups.label: All nine, global
items: ElevenLabs voice is never "live" — "built, one key away". The live voice is Deepgram.
The 3D backdrop is a technical grid. No panorama, no photographic workshop scene.
Dropbox folder sync is "built, deploying", not deployed.
Never quote a running ledger total without the date beside it.
Never call 13,537 "manuals" — distinct fetchable PDFs is 14,770.
Never call 4,081 and 1,489 the same number.
There is no checkout. "Live prices", never "buy".

notes: Presenter-only. The audience sees the end card.

What we got wrong, if asked: the name-based station join; shipping the first reduction without the ISD quality filter; and reading "−45 … −25 °C" as a promise of −45 °C when it is a mixing range — 188 manuals were briefly wrong in the safe-looking direction, which is the worse direction.
